The competitor's strategy of filing for multiple patents on next-generation wireless communication is a high-impact move designed to create a defensive moat and potentially a temporary monopoly. By securing intellectual property rights, Theta GmbH aims to block our direct access to these specific technologies, which will likely increase our R&D costs and time-to-market. We may be forced to invest in alternative technical pathways or engage in costly licensing negotiations, which could strain our resources and delay product launches. This maneuver signals that Theta GmbH is aggressively positioning itself as a key player in the wireless communications space, and we must respond by accelerating our own innovation pipeline or exploring cross-licensing opportunities to mitigate these barriers.
